about: Every external source, data store, processing step and page of cosh, and the flows between them. Read by web/dataflow.html, scripts/dataflow.py (check, plan) and `python3 -m cosh update`. Field meanings and the flow rules: docs/data-architecture.md. Keep it current: CLAUDE.md, Conventions. Building and deploying the site (npm run build; the Pages workflow on push) is not a data step and isn't listed.

sources.name: Chromium Gerrit
sources.purpose: Code review of chromium/src: CL listings over REST, each CL's review comments and events as its NoteDb ref, and its uploaded patch sets.
sources.access: Anonymous; every request carries the contact e-mail (data/private/settings.json or COSH_CONTACT).
sources.load_rules: REST serial, at least 1 s apart; NoteDb in batches of 200 refspecs, one fetch at a time; patch sets with glob refspecs only (never ls-remote or blobs by id), up to 7 fetches at once, pausing together on a 429. Backoff on 429/5xx; one extractor at a time (data/private/extract.lock).
sources.coverage: chromium/src main (master before 2021-05): CLs closed 2017-W27 .. 2026-W44 plus an open-CL snapshot; patch sets of reviewed CLs closed 2023-W26 .. 2026-W44. The approved ranges are config/approved.json, which the fetchers enforce.
sources.notes: Three channels of one host: REST (listings, accounts), NoteDb (refs/changes/NN/N/meta) and patch-set refs (refs/changes/NN/N/<ps>).

sources.name: Chromium git
sources.purpose: Chromium's git history on main: commits, authors, files touched, footers and file contents.
sources.access: Anonymous git over HTTPS with the contact e-mail; main only, no tags.
sources.load_rules: One fetch of main at a time, under data/private/extract.lock. Other branches or repos need approval.
sources.coverage: All of main, with full blobs (approved 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07).

sources.name: Affiliations file
sources.purpose: Dated e-mail-to-employer overrides used to attribute each person to an organisation.
sources.access: Anonymous GET with the contact headers.
sources.load_rules: One small request per process that builds an OrgResolver; no approval needed. COSH_AFFILIATIONS_OFFLINE=1 skips it.

sources.name: Claude
sources.purpose: Labels and scores text that rules can't: addressed threads, comment tone, AI-written descriptions, coaching reports.
sources.access: The user's Claude Max login; untrusted text only through cosh.sandbox.Sandbox (no tools, scrubbed env, bwrap jail).
sources.load_rules: Costs Max usage: size each run (--week, --max-threads, --dry-run) first. Not Gerrit load, so calls may run in parallel.
sources.coverage: Haiku for bulk labels; Opus for audits and coaching reports.

sources.name: Cloudflare Radar
sources.purpose: Daily share of human web requests per browser (all devices, and iOS alone) and per OS.
sources.access: API token in CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, from `source ~/.secrets/cosh/secrets.sh`; never printed or committed.
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 1 s apart; complete quarters are never refetched. A weekly update is about 3 requests.
sources.coverage: 2023-06-26 (Radar's first data) to the day of the last run.

sources.name: Chromium issue tracker
sources.purpose: Metadata (type, priority, severity, component, status) of the bugs named in commit footers and security release notes.
sources.access: Anonymous POST to an undocumented endpoint; restricted bugs are silently left out (about 46% of asked IDs are visible).
sources.load_rules: Searches serial with no wait, 50 IDs each; backs off 5/15/30 min on 429, 5xx or network errors; stops on a captcha.
sources.coverage: 147,407 bug IDs from Bug:/Fixed: footers on main since 2023-07-01 and from Chrome Releases security fixes.

sources.name: Monorail stubs
sources.purpose: Redirect pages that map pre-2024 Monorail bug IDs to their new tracker IDs.
sources.load_rules: Up to 4 at once with no wait; any 429, 5xx or network error stops all workers and backs off.
sources.coverage: All 21,267 Monorail-era IDs wanted as of 2026-11-08.

sources.name: Chrome Releases blog
sources.purpose: Release posts listing each security fix's CVE, bug ID and severity.
sources.access: Anonymous GET; post bodies are parsed by regex only and never shown to a model.
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 2 s apart, 150 posts per page; cached pages are not refetched without --refresh.

steps.command: python3 -m cosh backfill --weeks 1 --newest <week> --go; python3 -m cosh extract-open
steps.purpose: Fetches closed CLs week by week (listings over REST, review history as NoteDb refs) and snapshots the open ones.
steps.incremental: Skips listing windows and refs already fetched; a finished week is skipped. Each extract-open run lists open CLs updated since the last complete snapshot.
steps.duration: about 22 min per week (18.8 h for 52 weeks)
steps.approval: Only weeks in config/approved.json (2017-W27 .. 2026-W44); the command refuses others. A newer week needs the user's approval, then an edit to that file.
steps.notes: backfill --weeks N runs many weeks, newest first; long runs go in a systemd user service (CLAUDE.md). backfill also derives each week it finishes (cosh.derive for that week), so derived.sqlite stays current between full derives. Never run alongside another extractor.

steps.purpose: Copies Chromium's affiliations file into config/ when it has changed.
steps.incremental: Rewrites only on a change.
steps.duration: seconds
steps.notes: Every command that attributes orgs (summarize, comments-collect, review-feedback, balance-publish) also runs it by itself first; COSH_AFFILIATIONS_OFFLINE=1 stops that.

steps.purpose: Reduces every CL's listing and NoteDb comments to facts.
steps.incremental: Not incremental: a full run re-reads every CL. `--week W` does one week.
steps.duration: under 52 min for 1.6M CLs; 11.5 min for 775k
steps.cost_source: File times of the 2026-11-12 run (upper bound); docs/plan.md, 2026-11-05
steps.notes: Opens raw.sqlite read-only, so it is safe beside an extractor. Main's commits are in commits.sqlite (step commits), not here.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku label the threads the regex doesn't settle as addressed or not.
steps.incremental: Only threads with no label for the current classifier and input hash; saved per batch, so it resumes.
steps.duration: about 11 min per week; 41 min per year at 8 calls at once
steps.token_cost: about 0.95M Haiku tokens per week ($0.22); 25.6M per year ($6)
steps.approval: Costs Max usage: check --dry-run first (it underestimates by about a third). No labels for 2017 .. 2021.
steps.notes: A week shows the addressed metric only once it is 99% labelled, so the site's default metric needs this for each new week.

steps.purpose: Aggregates the facts and labels into the Value Exchange summaries for every fetched week.
steps.incremental: Rewrites every file for all weeks.
steps.notes: It runs update-affiliations first by itself (its only network use), so config/affiliations.json5 may change too. It reads the raw stores for the example threads' text.

steps.purpose: Lossless housekeeping of the NoteDb repo: packs refs and indexes its packs, so reads stay fast.
steps.incremental: Deletes nothing.
steps.duration: 41 min for the chunked repack of 3,823 packs into 14
steps.approval: Never prune. The chunked repack keeps the old packs until a person has checked the new ones.
steps.notes: For thousands of packs use scripts/notedb_chunked_repack.sh (700 MB groups); a whole-repo repack runs out of memory.

steps.purpose: Audits the addressed classifier against Opus, and the earlier research that chose the classifier and the Commits metric.
steps.duration: 32 Opus calls for 800 threads
steps.notes: scripts/comment_classifier.py still carries an older copy of the prompt than cosh/classify.py.

steps.purpose: Fetches chromium/src main into the shared clone, so new weeks' commits reach commits.sqlite.
steps.incremental: Fetches only what main gained since the last fetch.
steps.approval: main only (approved 2026-11-06); other branches or repos need approval.
steps.notes: The clone's README says cosh does these fetches. Run it before `cosh commits` when a new week is processed.

steps.purpose: Appends main's new commits, with their files, line counts, LSC tags, OWNERS additions and repetition ratios, to the commits store.
steps.incremental: Appends the commits landed since its last run; seconds when nothing is new.
steps.duration: about 1 h 50 min from empty (1.5 h of git log, then 20 min of OWNERS diffs and repetition ratios with 4 processes); seconds when nothing is new
steps.notes: Run it after the shared clone gains commits; nothing in cosh updates the clone. It replaces `cosh.balance git`, derive's commits tables and the hand-made balance inputs.

steps.purpose: Fetches every patch set of reviewed CLs, newest first, into the patch-set repo.
steps.incremental: Resumable. A CL is fetched again when Gerrit has more patch sets than were fetched (cosh-fetched.txt records the count).
steps.duration: 72 s per 1,000 CLs
steps.approval: Only reviewed CLs in config/approved.json's range (closed 2023-06-26 .. 2026-11-02); the command refuses an earlier --since. Up to 7 fetches at once (approved 2026-11-07).
steps.notes: Repack afterwards in groups with the two scripts; never prune.

steps.purpose: Fetches the Radar quarters that are missing or incomplete and rewrites the browser-share CSV.
steps.incremental: Complete quarters are skipped; `--offline` rebuilds the CSV from the cache alone.
steps.duration: about 3 requests, a few seconds
steps.approval: Approved. Never print or commit the token.

steps.command: python3 -m cosh.sentiment collect --missing (or --week <weeks>; --sample 0.05 --name sample-5pct for the trend's sample)
steps.purpose: Renders each week's review comments with their thread context and who wrote them, ready for scoring.
steps.incremental: Rewrites the week files it is given.
steps.duration: about 25 s per week; 2 min for the 5% sample
steps.notes: --missing collects every fetched week since the oldest week file that has no file yet. It refreshes the affiliations file first, like every command that attributes people (its only network use).

steps.purpose: Has Haiku score each rendered comment's tone and AI friction, in the sandbox.
steps.incremental: Skips comments already scored under the same prompt; saved per batch.
steps.duration: 3 to 4 min per week; 37 min for the 5% sample
steps.token_cost: about $1.25 of Haiku per week; 21.9M tokens ($5.48) for the 5% sample
steps.approval: Costs Max usage: size runs with --name or --week.

steps.purpose: Writes every Review Tone file from the newest year of fully scored weeks.
steps.incremental: Rewrites every file. Screening verdicts are cached in sentiment.sqlite, so only new comments cost model calls.
steps.token_cost: small, not measured; nothing once the cache has the comments
steps.approval: Publishes names for praise only; never negative figures per person or org (docs/sentiment.md).
steps.notes: The window follows the data: the newest run of up to 52 consecutive fully scored weeks (sentiment.scored_weeks). It also writes the screening cache (sentiment.sqlite's screens), which is not drawn as an output so the scores keep one writer.

steps.purpose: Scores a prompt version against the 261 gold comments, to tune the prompt.
Reads each CL's uploads, attention-set changes and Code-Review votes from NoteDb.
steps.incremental: Reads CLs not yet read and CLs whose meta ref's tip moved since (replacing their rows); CLs without a ref are looked for again next time.
steps.duration: 35.5 min (330 CLs/s, sharing the box with another git walk) for 716k CLs from empty

steps.purpose: Diffs each patch set against the next to measure rework during review.
steps.incremental: Only CLs without a result; CLs whose patch sets aren't fetched get none.
steps.duration: about 25 min as three shards

steps.purpose: Joins the stages into one row per CL.
steps.incremental: Rebuilds the whole table.
steps.duration: about 2 min for 1.14M CLs

steps.purpose: Lists the commits whose messages mark them as AI-assisted.
steps.duration: about 1 min

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_ai_predict.py build && nice -n 5 python3 scripts/balance_ai_predict.py score --since 2025-07-01
steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku estimate, for each CL description, whether it was AI-written.
steps.incremental: `score` resumes: descriptions already scored are skipped.
steps.duration: 116 min for 171,804 CLs at 8 calls at once

steps.purpose: Groups contributors' half-years into activity patterns and trajectories (k-means over private per-person panels), and maps the patterns.
steps.incremental: Recomputes everything.
steps.duration: about 10 min
steps.notes: An analysis kept as an input of balance-publish (its per-person people.json stays private); rerun it before a publish when the clusters should follow new data.

steps.purpose: Writes the Review Balance page's three files whole, from empty, by running each dataset's compute function in the order its STEPS list records.
steps.incremental: Recomputes everything; --steps a,b reruns only those steps and reuses the others' results in data/private/scratch/balance-publish/steps/.
steps.duration: about 8 min, about 5 GB of memory at most (one step at a time)
steps.notes: Its window ends at balance_publish.DATA_END (2026-11-01; D3 decides whether it follows new weeks). --check rebuilds into the scratch directory and compares with the committed files, dataset by dataset. Reads balance_clusters/, chrome_releases/summary.json and review_roi/ as finished analyses; everything else is computed on each run.

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_analysis.py trends|growth|pipeline; scripts/balance_ai.py paired|did|footers; scripts/balance_person.py; scripts/balance_exemplars.py; scripts/balance_explore.py
steps.purpose: Exploratory analyses behind the balance docs: trends, AI effects, per-person career reports.
steps.duration: 3 to 5 min and several GB of memory each
steps.token_cost: small Haiku pilots, about $0.06 per 1,000 CLs
steps.notes: Results go into docs/balance*.md by hand. Network use is the model pilots only.

steps.purpose: Writes each person's review feedback against their peers, as files named by a hash of their address.
steps.incremental: Deletes and rewrites every file.
steps.duration: about 3 min (188 s on 2026-11-12), 3 GB of memory
steps.approval: Tone is praise only (docs/plan.md, ground rule 5).
steps.notes: Computes its per-CL facts (owner, status, Gerrit size, landed commit, lines per directory) from derived.sqlite and commits.sqlite (cosh.cl_facts). Earlier commits count from 2008. Its tone year is Review Tone's (sentiment.scored_weeks). It refreshes the affiliations file first (its only network use). `npm run serve` picks the new files up a few seconds after the run ends.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Opus write a private coaching report from one person's recent review threads.
steps.incremental: `--reuse` rebuilds the report from the saved reply without a new call.
steps.duration: about 1 min per report
steps.approval: Costs Max usage; reports are never published.

steps.command: python3 scripts/review_roi_table.py ...; review_roi_part1.py; review_roi_part2.py; review_roi_blame.py; review_roi_reverts.py; review_roi_substance.py
steps.purpose: The review-ROI studies: whether review feedback predicts later reverts, bug-fixing commits and security bugs; and the addressed index against the feedback index.
steps.duration: about 1 h; the full blame runs were estimated at 10 to 16 CPU hours
steps.token_cost: Haiku pilots only: 274 tokens per thread, 200 threads
steps.notes: The scripts write to data/private/scratch/review_roi/ by default; the results balance-publish reads are copied into data/private/review_roi/ by hand (the addressed ones as addressed_cl.json, addressed_blame.json, addressed_people.json). This is the only path by which bug-tracker data reaches a page.

steps.command: python3 scripts/review_impact.py --weeks 2026-W36:2026-W44 --out threads.jsonl; python3 scripts/review_impact_stats.py threads.jsonl
steps.purpose: Early study of which review threads change the CL, behind docs/review-impact.md.
steps.duration: about 25 s

steps.purpose: Fetches the Chrome Releases feed, parses its security fixes and joins them to their fixing commits on main.
steps.incremental: Fetches only pages it lacks, so the newest page goes stale without --refresh; parse and join recompute.
steps.duration: about 1 min of fetching (26 requests)

steps.purpose: Lists the bug IDs to ask for, from commit footers on main and the security fixes.
steps.incremental: Recomputes the wanted table.
steps.duration: about 10 s

steps.command: nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs fetch --go && nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs monorail --go && nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs fetch --go
steps.purpose: Asks the tracker for every wanted bug not asked yet, maps old Monorail IDs, then asks for those too.
steps.incremental: Only IDs never asked; `fetch --retry-missing` re-asks invisible ones after 30 days. `parse` rebuilds the bugs table from raw/ offline.
steps.duration: about 1.5 h in all: 2,906 searches and 21,267 stub lookups
steps.approval: Approved 2026-11-08 for bugs in footers since 2023-07-01 and security fixes. Other trackers or b: bugs need approval.
